plan.title: Add budget_used column to departments with a default of 0

forward_steps.description: Add budget_used column to departments table with a default of 0. SQLite will set existing rows to 0 via the default, satisfying the NOT NULL constraint.
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE departments ADD COLUMN budget_used REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

forward_steps.description: Backfill any existing rows where budget_used might be NULL to ensure all rows have budget_used = 0. This is a safety step in case the SQLite version did not apply the default to existing rows.
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE departments SET budget_used = 0 WHERE budget_used IS NULL;

rollback_steps.description: Recreate the departments table without the budget_used column, copying all original data back, then drop the modified table and rename. Also re-establish any indexes or foreign key relationships.
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE departments_backup AS SELECT id, name, budget FROM departments; DROP TABLE departments; ALTER TABLE departments_backup RENAME TO departments;

rollback_steps.description: No data reversal needed for the backfill UPDATE since the column itself is dropped in rollback step 1. This is a no-op placeholder confirming the UPDATE is fully reversed by the column removal.

plan.validation_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS: all rows have budget_used = 0' ELSE 'FAIL: some rows have budget_used != 0 or NULL' END AS result FROM departments WHERE budget_used IS NULL OR budget_used != 0; SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN budget_used = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_with_zero FROM departments;

plan.title: Add end_date column to projects

forward_steps.description: Add nullable end_date column to projects table
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN end_date TEXT NULL;

forward_steps.description: Backfill end_date for completed projects using start_date as a placeholder (sets end_date to start_date where no real end date is known)
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = start_date WHERE status = 'completed' AND end_date IS NULL;

forward_steps.description: Backfill end_date for cancelled projects using start_date as a placeholder (sets end_date to start_date where no real end date is known)
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = start_date WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND end_date IS NULL;

forward_steps.description: Verify active projects have NULL end_date (no SQL change, audit only — sets active project end_dates to NULL in case any were inadvertently set)
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = NULL WHERE status = 'active';

rollback_steps.description: Clear end_date values backfilled for active projects (reverse step 4 — restore any overwritten values; since active rows were set to NULL this is a no-op in practice)
rollback_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = NULL WHERE status = 'active';

rollback_steps.description: Clear end_date backfill for cancelled projects
rollback_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = NULL WHERE status = 'cancelled';

rollback_steps.description: Clear end_date backfill for completed projects
rollback_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET end_date = NULL WHERE status = 'completed';

rollback_steps.description: Remove end_date column by recreating projects table without it
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE projects_backup AS SELECT id, name, dept_id, start_date, status FROM projects; DROP TABLE projects; ALTER TABLE projects_backup RENAME TO projects;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE status = 'active' AND end_date IS NOT NULL) AS active_with_end_date_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE status = 'completed' AND end_date IS NULL) AS completed_missing_end_date_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND end_date IS NULL) AS cancelled_missing_end_date_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('projects') WHERE name = 'end_date') AS column_exists;

plan.title: Add unique department_code column to departments

forward_steps.description: Add department_code column as nullable TEXT (no constraints yet) to allow backfill

forward_steps.description: Backfill department_code for all 5 existing departments using unique codes based on their id
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE departments SET department_code = CASE id WHEN 1 THEN 'ENG' WHEN 2 THEN 'SALES' WHEN 3 THEN 'MKT' WHEN 4 THEN 'HR' WHEN 5 THEN 'RES' ELSE 'DEPT' || CAST(id AS TEXT) END;

forward_steps.description: Verify all departments have a non-null department_code before applying constraints (guard check via assertion pattern)
forward_steps.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'OK' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS check_result FROM departments WHERE department_code IS NULL;

forward_steps.description: Recreate departments table with department_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE constraint (SQLite requires table rebuild for constraints)
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE departments_new (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, budget REAL, department_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);

forward_steps.description: Copy all data from old departments table into new table
forward_steps.sql: INSERT INTO departments_new (id, name, budget, department_code) SELECT id, name, budget, department_code FROM departments;

forward_steps.description: Drop the old departments table
forward_steps.sql: DROP TABLE departments;

forward_steps.description: Rename departments_new to departments
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE departments_new RENAME TO departments;

rollback_steps.description: Recreate the original departments table without department_code
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE departments_rollback (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, budget REAL);

rollback_steps.description: Copy data back excluding department_code column
rollback_steps.sql: INSERT INTO departments_rollback (id, name, budget) SELECT id, name, budget FROM departments;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the migrated departments table

rollback_steps.description: Rename rollback table back to departments
rollback_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE departments_rollback RENAME TO departments;

rollback_steps.description: No action needed — table rebuild in step 4 forward already removed the nullable column; data is restored to original shape
No action needed — backfill update is undone by the table recreation above

plan.title: Add manager_id self-reference to employees

forward_steps.description: Add nullable manager_id column to employees table as a self-referential foreign key. SQLite allows adding a column with a FK reference to the same table; NULL values indicate top-level employees with no manager.
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN manager_id INTEGER NULL REFERENCES employees(id);

forward_steps.description: Verify all non-NULL manager_id values reference valid employee ids (data integrity check). This UPDATE is a no-op placeholder ensuring any stale/invalid references are nullified before relying on the constraint.
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE employees SET manager_id = NULL WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL AND manager_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees);

forward_steps.description: Create an index on employees.manager_id to support efficient hierarchical queries (e.g. finding all direct reports).
forward_steps.sql: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_employees_manager_id ON employees(manager_id);

rollback_steps.description: Drop the index on manager_id before removing the column.
rollback_steps.sql: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_employees_manager_id;

rollback_steps.description: Reverse the data integrity nullification step — no data to restore since it was only nullifying orphaned references.

Recreate the employees table without the manager_id column. SQLite does not support DROP COLUMN in older versions, so we use the standard table-rebuild approach: create new table, copy data, drop old, rename.
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE employees_backup AS SELECT id, name, dept_id, salary, hire_date FROM employees; DROP TABLE employees; CREATE TABLE employees ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept_id INTEGER REFERENCES departments(id), salary REAL, hire_date TEXT ); INSERT INTO employees (id, name, dept_id, salary, hire_date) SELECT id, name, dept_id, salary, hire_date FROM employees_backup; DROP TABLE employees_backup;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS: All manager_id values are valid (NULL or reference existing employee)' ELSE 'FAIL: Orphaned manager_id references detected' END AS result FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL AND manager_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees); SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) >= 0 THEN 'PASS: manager_id column exists on employees' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS column_check FROM pragma_table_info('employees') WHERE name = 'manager_id';

plan.title: Change assignments.hours from REAL to INTEGER (truncating decimals)

forward_steps.description: Create a new assignments table with hours defined as INTEGER
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE assignments_new (employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL, project_id INTEGER NOT NULL, role TEXT, hours INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (employee_id, project_id), FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id), FOREIGN KEY (project_id) REFERENCES projects(id));

forward_steps.description: Copy all rows from assignments into assignments_new, truncating hours to INTEGER using CAST
forward_steps.sql: INSERT INTO assignments_new (employee_id, project_id, role, hours) SELECT employee_id, project_id, role, CAST(hours AS INTEGER) FROM assignments;

forward_steps.description: Verify no rows were lost before dropping the old table
Drop the original assignments table
forward_steps.sql: DROP TABLE assignments;

forward_steps.description: Rename assignments_new to assignments
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE assignments_new RENAME TO assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Rename current assignments (INTEGER hours) back to assignments_new to free the name
rollback_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE assignments RENAME TO assignments_new;

rollback_steps.description: Recreate the original assignments table with hours as REAL
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE assignments (employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL, project_id INTEGER NOT NULL, role TEXT, hours REAL, PRIMARY KEY (employee_id, project_id), FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(id), FOREIGN KEY (project_id) REFERENCES projects(id));

rollback_steps.description: Copy rows back from assignments_new into the restored assignments table, casting INTEGER hours back to REAL
rollback_steps.sql: INSERT INTO assignments (employee_id, project_id, role, hours) SELECT employee_id, project_id, role, CAST(hours AS REAL) FROM assignments_new;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the temporary assignments_new table used during rollback
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE assignments_new;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments) AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('assignments') WHERE name = 'hours' AND type = 'INTEGER') = 1 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments WHERE hours != CAST(hours AS INTEGER)) = 0 THEN 'MIGRATION OK' ELSE 'MIGRATION FAILED' END AS result;

plan.title: Normalize role in assignments into a lookup table

forward_steps.description: Create the roles lookup table with id and unique name columns
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE roles (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);

forward_steps.description: Populate roles table with all distinct role values from assignments
forward_steps.sql: INSERT INTO roles (name) SELECT DISTINCT role FROM assignments WHERE role IS NOT NULL;

forward_steps.description: Add role_id column to assignments table as a nullable integer (FK to roles will be enforced logically)
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE assignments ADD COLUMN role_id INTEGER REFERENCES roles(id);

forward_steps.description: Backfill role_id in assignments by joining on matching role name in roles
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE assignments SET role_id = (SELECT id FROM roles WHERE roles.name = assignments.role);

forward_steps.description: Recreate assignments table without the role TEXT column, keeping role_id FK, to effectively drop the role column (SQLite does not support DROP COLUMN in older versions; use table rebuild)
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE assignments_new (employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id), project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id), role_id INTEGER REFERENCES roles(id), hours REAL, PRIMARY KEY (employee_id, project_id));

forward_steps.description: Copy all data from assignments into assignments_new
forward_steps.sql: INSERT INTO assignments_new (employee_id, project_id, role_id, hours) SELECT employee_id, project_id, role_id, hours FROM assignments;

forward_steps.description: Drop the old assignments table
forward_steps.sql: DROP TABLE assignments;

forward_steps.description: Rename assignments_new to assignments
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE assignments_new RENAME TO assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Recreate the original assignments table with role TEXT column instead of role_id
rollback_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE assignments_old (employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id), project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id), role TEXT, hours REAL, PRIMARY KEY (employee_id, project_id));

rollback_steps.description: Copy data back from assignments to assignments_old, restoring role TEXT by joining with roles
rollback_steps.sql: INSERT INTO assignments_old (employee_id, project_id, role, hours) SELECT a.employee_id, a.project_id, r.name, a.hours FROM assignments a LEFT JOIN roles r ON a.role_id = r.id;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the current assignments table (with role_id)
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Rename assignments_old back to assignments
rollback_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE assignments_old RENAME TO assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the roles lookup table
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE roles;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments WHERE role_id IS NULL) = 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM roles) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.name) FROM roles r) AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments a LEFT JOIN roles r ON a.role_id = r.id WHERE r.id IS NULL) = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('assignments') WHERE name = 'role') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('assignments') WHERE name = 'role_id') THEN 'MIGRATION_OK' ELSE 'MIGRATION_FAILED' END AS result;

plan.title: Create salary_history table and backfill from current employee salaries

forward_steps.description: Create the salary_history table with autoincrement primary key, foreign key to employees, salary, effective_date, and recorded_at columns
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE salary_history (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id), salary REAL NOT NULL, effective_date TEXT NOT NULL, recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL);

forward_steps.description: Backfill salary_history with each employee's current salary, using hire_date as effective_date and the current timestamp as recorded_at
forward_steps.sql: INSERT INTO salary_history (employee_id, salary, effective_date, recorded_at) SELECT id, salary, hire_date, datetime('now') FROM employees;

rollback_steps.description: Remove all backfilled rows from salary_history (reverses the INSERT...SELECT backfill)
rollback_steps.sql: DELETE FROM salary_history;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the salary_history table entirely (reverses table creation)
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS salary_history;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM salary_history) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees) AS row_counts_match, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM salary_history WHERE employee_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees)) = 0 AS no_orphan_records, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM salary_history sh JOIN employees e ON sh.employee_id = e.id WHERE sh.salary != e.salary OR sh.effective_date != e.hire_date) = 0 AS salary_and_date_match, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM salary_history WHERE recorded_at IS NULL OR recorded_at = '') = 0 AS recorded_at_populated;

plan.title: Delete cancelled projects and clean up orphan assignments

forward_steps.description: Create a backup table for cancelled projects before deletion
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _backup_cancelled_projects AS SELECT * FROM projects WHERE status = 'cancelled';

forward_steps.description: Create a backup table for orphan assignments referencing cancelled projects before deletion
forward_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _backup_cancelled_assignments AS SELECT a.* FROM assignments a INNER JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id WHERE p.status = 'cancelled';

forward_steps.description: Delete all assignments that reference cancelled projects (FK order: child before parent)
forward_steps.sql: DELETE FROM assignments WHERE project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE status = 'cancelled');

forward_steps.description: Delete all projects with status='cancelled'
forward_steps.sql: DELETE FROM projects WHERE status = 'cancelled';

rollback_steps.description: Restore cancelled projects from backup table
rollback_steps.sql: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO projects SELECT * FROM _backup_cancelled_projects;

rollback_steps.description: Restore orphan assignments from backup table
rollback_steps.sql: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO assignments SELECT * FROM _backup_cancelled_assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the assignments backup table
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _backup_cancelled_assignments;

rollback_steps.description: Drop the projects backup table
rollback_steps.sql: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _backup_cancelled_projects;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE status = 'cancelled') AS remaining_cancelled_projects, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments WHERE project_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM projects)) AS orphan_assignments, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM _backup_cancelled_projects) AS backed_up_projects, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM _backup_cancelled_assignments) AS backed_up_assignments;

plan.title: Add priority column to projects with CHECK constraint

forward_steps.description: Add priority column to projects table with NOT NULL, DEFAULT 3, and CHECK constraint (priority BETWEEN 1 AND 5). SQLite will populate all existing rows with the default value of 3.
forward_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK(priority BETWEEN 1 AND 5);

forward_steps.description: Verify all existing rows have priority = 3 (the default). This is a data integrity check step with no schema change.
forward_steps.sql: UPDATE projects SET priority = 3 WHERE priority IS NULL;

forward_steps.description: Confirm no rows violate the CHECK constraint (priority BETWEEN 1 AND 5). Raises an error implicitly if any out-of-range value exists by attempting a no-op update that would trigger the constraint check.
forward_steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invalid_priority_count FROM projects WHERE priority < 1 OR priority > 5 OR priority IS NULL;

rollback_steps.description: Rollback step 3: No schema change was made; nothing to undo for the validation query.
Rollback step 2: No data was structurally changed beyond what the column addition did; the UPDATE of NULLs is moot once the column is dropped.

Rollback step 1: SQLite does not support DROP COLUMN directly in older versions, so recreate projects table without the priority column, copy data, drop old table, and rename. Uses a transaction for safety.
rollback_steps.sql: BEGIN TRANSACTION; CREATE TABLE projects_backup (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept_id INTEGER REFERENCES departments(id), start_date TEXT, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('active','completed','cancelled'))); INSERT INTO projects_backup (id, name, dept_id, start_date, status) SELECT id, name, dept_id, start_date, status FROM projects; DROP TABLE projects; ALTER TABLE projects_backup RENAME TO projects; COMMIT;

plan.validation_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'MIGRATION OK: all projects have valid priority' ELSE 'MIGRATION FAILED: some projects have invalid or missing priority' END AS result FROM projects WHERE priority IS NULL OR priority < 1 OR priority > 5;
